comparison.subtitle: See how ImgSplit stacks up against traditional image editing tools.
comparison.feature1Desc: ImgSplit runs entirely in your browser — no downloads, no installations, no server uploads. Your images stay on your device at all times, ensuring complete privacy. Traditional tools like Photoshop require expensive subscriptions and heavy desktop software.
comparison.feature2Desc: Drag split lines with snap alignment for exact pixel positioning. Unlike basic online croppers that only let you select a single region, ImgSplit divides the entire image into multiple pieces simultaneously — preserving every pixel.
comparison.feature3Desc: Upload PNG, JPG, or WebP images and download your split pieces in the same high-quality format. Each piece retains the original resolution with zero compression artifacts — what you see is exactly what you get.
comparison.feature4Desc: Works on any modern browser — Chrome, Firefox, Safari, or Edge. Split images on your desktop, tablet, or phone with the same full-featured experience. No app store downloads needed.
comparison.feature5Desc: Whether you are an e-commerce seller splitting product photos, a designer slicing mockups, a social media manager creating grid posts, or a student preparing presentation materials — ImgSplit adapts to your workflow. Add up to 20 horizontal and 20 vertical lines to create any layout you need.
comparison.feature6Desc: ImgSplit is open-source software published on GitHub. Anyone can inspect the code, verify our privacy claims, and contribute improvements. Your images never leave your device; we use anonymous product analytics (Umami) and error monitoring (Sentry); no advertising cookies, no personal identity tracking.

metadata.title: About ImgSplit — Free Online Image Splitting Tool
metadata.description: Learn about ImgSplit — a free, open-source, browser-based image splitting tool built by ZooHero. Privacy-first, no upload needed.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.description: ImgSplit was built to solve a simple problem: splitting images shouldn't require expensive software or uploading files to unknown servers. We believe image editing tools should be free, private, and accessible to everyone.
mission.highlight: Every image you process stays on your device — always.

creator.title: Built by
creator.name: ZooHero
creator.bio: Full-stack developer passionate about building free, privacy-first web tools. ImgSplit is open source and built with Next.js, React, and the Canvas API.

tech.title: How It Works
tech.description: ImgSplit runs entirely in your browser using the HTML5 Canvas API. When you split an image, the processing happens locally on your device — no server round-trips, no uploads. Your images never leave your device. We use anonymous product analytics (Umami) and error monitoring (Sentry) to improve the tool. This architecture ensures zero latency, complete privacy, and works offline after the initial page load.

items.browserDesc: All image processing uses the HTML5 Canvas API. Your images never leave your device.
items.opensourceDesc: Full source code available on GitHub. Inspect, contribute, or fork — it's all transparent.
items.privacyDesc: Your images never leave your device. We use anonymous product analytics and error monitoring — but we never analyze your image content. No advertising cookies, no personal identity tracking, no server-side image processing.
items.freeDesc: No paywalls, no premium tiers, no signup required. ImgSplit will always be free.

brand.title: Brand Notice
brand.description: ImgSplit (imgsplit.com) is not affiliated with the npm package @imgsplit/core, github.com/imgsplit/imgsplit, or imgsplit.com.tr. The official source repository is github.com/ZooHero500/imgsplit.

hero.description: A one-time on-device model download lets a browser Web Worker cut the subject out. Your photo is not uploaded — processing stays on this computer.

features.item1Title: Local AI in a Web Worker
features.item1Desc: After the model is cached, inference runs in a browser Worker. The image bitmap never goes to ImgSplit’s servers.
features.item2Desc: The first run fetches the local RMBG model and stores it in this browser’s cache. Later edits usually skip the download.
features.item3Desc: Set alpha cutoff, shrink/expand, and feather before you run — then re-remove if you change the sliders.
features.item4Desc: Download a transparent PNG or WebP, or a JPEG on white. Batch mode queues several images and zips the ready ones.

steps.step1Desc: PNG, JPEG, or WebP, up to 20MB. Add more files if you want a batch queue.
steps.step2Desc: If this browser has no cache yet, the first run downloads the local model. The photo still stays on the device.
steps.step3Desc: Adjust leftover haze, subject inset, and softness, then run or re-run removal in the Worker.
steps.step4Desc: Save a transparent PNG/WebP or a white-background JPEG. Ready batch items download as a ZIP.

faq.subtitle: What “local AI in the browser” means for your photos.
faq.a1: No. The image is decoded and processed in this tab’s Web Worker. Only the public model files are downloaded, not your photo.
faq.q2: Why does the first run download a model?
faq.a2: Background removal needs a local ONNX model (RMBG). It is fetched once, cached in the browser, and reused. Your images are not part of that download.
faq.a3: Transparent PNG, transparent WebP, or JPEG with a white background. Quality applies to WebP and JPEG.
faq.a4: Yes. Add more images to the queue, set edge cleanup once, then start batch removal and download a ZIP of finished cutouts.

faq.subtitle: Practical details about browser-side compression and format conversion.
faq.q1: Which formats can I convert between?
faq.a1: PNG, JPEG, and WebP. You can compress in the same format or convert — for example JPEG to WebP — without uploading the file.
faq.a2: No. Compression and conversion run entirely in your browser. ImgSplit never receives the files.
faq.q3: How does the quality slider work?
faq.a3: For JPEG and WebP, 10–100 controls lossy compression. Higher keeps more detail and a larger file. PNG is lossless, so quality does not apply.
faq.q4: Can I compress many images at once?
faq.a4: Yes. Add multiple files, wait until each shows a result, then download a ZIP of the compressed images.
